source_title: daveebbelaar/bama: BAMA: Build Any Mac App. Agent skills to research, clone, design, build, optimize, and test native macOS apps with Swift and SwiftUI. - GitHub
source_excerpt:
See an app you like. Rebuild it as your own native Mac app.
Agent skills that take a native macOS app from idea to your Dock. Swift and SwiftUI. Local data. No Xcode GUI.
Quick start · How it works · Skills · Specs · Install
Not sure where to start? Type /bama . It looks at your project and picks the next skill.
Your agent opens the app you like and screenshots every screen. It writes a screen index.
It turns the screens into user stories with checkable acceptance criteria, in milestones.
It builds one story per commit. Before each commit it snapshots every page in light and dark mode and runs the tests.
Not sure what to build? specs/ has 12 build plans for small Mac apps: a window snapper, a window switcher, a launcher, clipboard history, screenshots, a screen recorder, and more. I took them apart from Onyx, my own menu bar app. Copy one into an empty folder and tell your agent:
Pick one route per agent. Two routes install every skill twice.
Uses skills.sh . Install all skills, or one with --skill .
Xcode 26 or later, for the Swift 6.2 toolchain (you never open it)
An agent that supports skills: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI
For clone on native apps: computer use (Claude Pro or Max)
The idea and the "any" promise come from REA: Reverse Engineer Anything by morluto. REA showed that an agent can reverse engineer any app. BAMA takes that idea to the Mac.
Skill format and writing rules follow Matt Pocock's skills and his writing-for-agents skill.
Works well with SwiftUI Pro by Paul Hudson and SwiftUI Expert by Antoine van der Lee.
BAMA: Build Any Mac App. Agent skills to research, clone, design, build, optimize, and test native macOS apps with Swift and SwiftUI.
